content: I've just created stable branches for both Mathlib and Std, with the intention that these will be updated to each new v4.X.0 tag on these repositories (i.e. the first moment at which the repository starts using the new toolchain).
@Mario Carneiro, would you mind adding a branch protection rule for stable on Std, so that only admins + me can push to it?
I will make a bit of an announcement song and dance about these when v4.2.0 lands next week.
std doesn't really use branch protection rules, except that main requires builds to pass
if you have write access you are already a privileged user under the std permissions model
Will 4.2.0 include the recent simp fixes?
@Patrick Massot, no, it won't. They will arrive on v4.3.0-rc1, probably next Monday, but will not become part of a stable release until the end of November.
(i.e. Mathlib and Std will hopefully have them on Monday)
The rule for v4.X.0 is that it is identical for v4.X.0-rcMAX. So v4.2.0 will be identical to the current v4.2.0-rc4 ( :fingers_crossed: for lake emergencies).
Ok, that's perfect. I don't care about stable releases, I only care about the version used by Mathlib.
I'm a bit concerned still that the recent changes to simp will require more follow up changes, so when they land I encourage everyone to stress test them. We can likely have an v4.3.0-rc2 to adjust.

Following up on #mathlib4 > Tagging commits in mathlib4, I noticed that batteries doesn't have a v4.29.1 tag and commit yet. Should we add that (and then bump stable to point there)? cc: @Joscha Mennicken
There are no changes from v4.29.0 so there is no need. It is harmless to add a new tag but would anyone use it?
LLM companies who are stuck on v4.29.1 because that's what their model writes might want to just "check out v4.29.1 of everything"
It's easier to use a fixed lake-manifest.json which stores all the right commits directly.
LLMs aside, there are humans who find it helpful for the git tags to be consistent across core/batteries/Mathlib.

I find it very helpful that I know what to upgrade my dependencies to without thinking when the eco system goes through its monthly forced version bump. I also find it helpful when conducting experiments across the eco system.

There's no harm adding a v4.29.1 tag but it would just point to v4.29.0. If you want a proper v4.29.1 tag with the correct lean-toolchain, that requires git surgery and I would defer to @Joscha Mennicken.
@Henrik Böving v4.29.1 is special since it is a patch release. The tags you (and I) need for monthly bumps are all there and correct.

François G. Dorais said:

that requires git surgery

How about

git switch --detach v4.29.0
# now upgrade toolchain to v4.29.1, and then
git commit -am "chore: bump toolchain to v4.29.1"
git tag v4.29.1
git push origin v4.29.1

(while ignoring the "detached HEAD" warnings, because we know what we're doing)

If by surgery you mean rewriting history then I think it's a bad idea.

I could do it but @Joscha Mennicken is the person in charge here, so I'm leaving non-trivial stuff to them.

The trivial thing I could do is just add a v4.29.1 tag pointing to v4.29.0. After all, it doesn't matter what the lean-toolchain is in batteries since that's ignored by any project that imports batteries.

François G. Dorais said:

After all, it doesn't matter what the lean-toolchain is in batteries since that's ignored by any project that imports batteries.

These tags appear for instance in Mathlib's and CSLib's lake-manifest.json, so they are not completely ignored, right?

The lean-toolchain file is ignored: a project is built using only one toolchain.

As for the lake-manifest.json files, the rev commit stored there always has priority over the inputRev (which could be a tag, branch, or fixed commit from the input lakefile).

In other words, as I said before, 756e3321fd3b02a85ffda19fef789916223e578c is the right commit if your toolchain is v4.29.0 or v4.29.1. Whether you call it stable, v4.29.0 or v4.29.1 (which currently does not exist) is entirely cosmetic.

I've added a v4.29.1 tag pointing to 756e3321fd3b02a85ffda19fef789916223e578c. Keep in mind that this commit lists lean-toolchain as v4.29.0. As I explained, this is harmless and irrelevant for most use cases.

I think we should just do what @Snir Broshi wrote above, creating v4.29.1 off to the side of v4.29.0.

I guess this was never automated, but it has been done in the past, including for Mathlib, for patch releases.

But there is no need. All that would do is create a branch with v4.29.1 in the lean-toolchain but that has zero effect since the batteries lean-toolchain file is ignored by any project that imports batteries.
Also, v4.30.0 would not be built upon v4.29.1, which is weird. We should just wait for Josha to decide what to do.

I did the "branch off of v4.29.0 to create a commit tagged v4.29.1" for doc-gen4 because apparently some CI fails if this version didn't exist. It makes a bit more sense for doc-gen4 since it is fetched by the CI without being present in the project itself as a dependency. I wasn't sure which toolchain the CI would end up using, so I just bumped it in doc-gen4.

Regarding v4.30.0 not being built upon 4.29.1, this is already the case for mathlib's v4.29.1 anyways, which also branches off of v4.29.0 and just bumps the toolchain.

Originally when releasing v4.29.1, I had hoped that not many repos would need to be touched, but it seems like it might make sense to just blanket-release v4.29.1 bump commits (branching off of v4.29.0) since some tooling (and some users) seem to expect them.
